prompt:
The concepts of precision and accuracy are often illustrated using target analogies:
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Three circular target faces with concentric rings and a central bullseye representing the true value. Target A has five hit marks clustered closely together within the central bullseye. Target B has five hit marks clustered tightly together in the outer upper-right quadrant. Target C has five hit marks widely scattered across the target face, but positioned symmetrically such that their average position is the bullseye.]
Classify each target using the terms precise, not precise, accurate, not accurate, and justify each classification:
(a) Target A [1]
(b) Target B [1]
(c) Target C [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: Part (a): Precise and accurate; hits are closely grouped together (small spread) and close to the true value / bullseye.
Part (b): Precise but not accurate; hits are closely grouped together (small spread) but consistently displaced from the true value (systematic offset).
Part (c): Accurate but not precise; hits have large spread (low precision) but their average / central position aligns with the true value.

hints: Check position relative to the center for accuracy.
solution: (a) Precise and accurate: small spread and on target. (b) Precise but not accurate: small spread but shifted from target. (c) Accurate but not precise: large spread but centered on target.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) Target A: hits are close to each other (precise) and centered on bullseye (accurate).
(b) Target B: hits are tightly clustered together (precise) but far from bullseye (inaccurate).
(c) Target C: hits are widely dispersed (not precise) but their mean position is the bullseye (accurate).

provenance.independence_statement: Authored target-shooting analogy classifying three distinct precision-accuracy combinations.
